newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth CEO sees stiff competition.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth CEO sees stiff competition.

text.p: BellSouth Corp Chief Executive F. Duane Ackerman predicted on Monday that his company's home market would see some of the country's fiercest competition as telephone, wireless and cable-television markets began to merge this year.

To meet those challenges, he said in remarks prepared for a speech at a Rotary luncheon that BellSouth had negotiated 59 agreements allowing other companies, including AT&T Corp and MCI Communications Corp to resell services from its network.

The regional Bell holding company would extend its current Internet access service from a current 14 cities to 30 cities next month in a previously announced alliance with International Business Machines Corp.
Ackerman said BellSouth was on track with plans to begin offering digital wireless cable-television service in the Atlanta metro area late in the coming year.

BellSouth also hopes to begin offering long-distance telephone service to customers later this year, depending on when it wins regulatory approval by the Georgia Public Service Commission and the U.S. Federal Communications Commission, he said.
"Since Atlanta is such a leading communications city, it will see local competition faster than will many other cities," Ackerman said in his remarks.
"AT&T will be in here. So will MCI. MediaOne, a cable company, is gearing up to offer phone service. And more specialized companies are already focused on the business market."
